web.title: Next.js 16
web.description:
Ahead of our upcoming [Next.js Conf 2025](https://nextjs.org/conf), Next.js 16 is now available.

This release provides the latest improvements to Turbopack, caching, and the Next.js architecture.

- [**Turbopack (stable)**](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16#turbopack-stable): Default bundler for all apps with up to 5-10x faster Fast Refresh, and 2-5x faster builds

## [Copy link to heading](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16#new-features-and-improvements) New Features and Improvements
### [Copy link to heading](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16#logging-improvements) Logging Improvements
```
   ▲ Next.js 16 (Turbopack)

 ✓ Compiled successfully in 615ms
 ✓ Finished TypeScript in 1114ms
 ✓ Collecting page data in 208ms
 ✓ Generating static pages in 239ms
 ✓ Finalizing page optimization in 5ms
```

### [Copy link to heading](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16#developer-experience) Developer Experience
#### [Copy link to heading](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16#turbopack-stable) Turbopack (stable)
Turbopack has reached stability for both development and production builds, and is now the default bundler for all new Next.js projects.

With Turbopack, you can expect:

- 2–5× faster production builds
- Up to 10× faster Fast Refresh

We're making Turbopack the default to bring these performance gains to every Next.js developer, no configuration required. For apps with custom webpack setups, you can continue using webpack by running:

terminal

```
next dev --webpack
next build --webpack
```

#### [Copy link to heading](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16#turbopack-file-system-caching-beta) Turbopack File System Caching (beta)
```
const nextConfig = {
  experimental: {
    turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev: true,
  },
};

export default nextConfig;
```

### [Copy link to heading](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16#core-features--architecture) Core Features & Architecture
#### [Copy link to heading](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16#react-192-and-canary-features) React 19.2 and Canary Features
The App Router in Next.js 16 uses the latest React [Canary release](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries), which includes the newly released React 19.2 features and other features being incrementally stabilized.
